  <section class="home-section research-front" data-reveal aria-labelledby="research-front-title">
    <header class="section-heading section-heading-wide">
      <p>RESEARCH</p>
      <h2 id="research-front-title">Learning physical systems for control and optimization.</h2>
      <p>My research asks which physical variables a learned model must represent, how those states evolve under external forcing and incomplete observation, and which approximation errors change the resulting schedule, control action, or design. I study this question through probabilistic prediction, neural operators, closed-loop analysis, and constrained optimization.</p>
    </header>
    <div class="research-program-grid">
      <article class="research-thread theme-decision">
        <h3>Decision-focused forecasting under uncertainty</h3>
        <p>Probabilistic forecasts are trained and evaluated through the schedules, costs, and constraints they induce. Work on water-demand timing and uncertain pressure regression further identifies when prediction errors occur and which unobserved effects they represent.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="research-thread theme-operator">
        <h3>Neural operators for distributed dynamics</h3>
        <p>I study maps from initial conditions, geometry, boundary conditions, and forcing fields to spatiotemporal solutions. Field error, rollout error, and sensitivity error measure how accurately the learned operator represents the dynamics used in control and optimization.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="research-thread theme-physical">
        <h3>Learning-based control</h3>
        <p>I examine how approximation error accumulates over a control horizon and changes the selected action, closed-loop cost, and constraint violation. These quantities provide control-specific criteria for training and evaluating learned physical dynamics.</p>
      </article>
      <article class="research-thread theme-materials">
        <h3>Constrained optimization of physical systems</h3>
        <p>I study differentiable solution operators inside constrained design and operating problems, including experiment selection, process control, and materials design. Gradient accuracy and feasibility determine whether the learned model preserves the optimized decision.</p>
      </article>
    </div>
    <p class="section-link"><a href="/research/">Methods and research questions</a></p>
  </section>
